title: Absence of embodied misalignment and loss-of-control evaluations
body: Most surveyed work addresses accidents, misuse or attacks. Few studies address cases in which a model exhibits dangerous behaviour on its own, e.g. due to competing goals. EAPrivacy reports that agents prioritised task completion over a stated privacy constraint in up to 86% of cases. What Happens to the Goal? traces goal misgeneralization inside trained policies on navigation and manipulation tasks, but does not study frontier robot models. Goodhart in the Planner demonstrates reward hacking by a robot planner in simulation. Loss-of-control scenarios, in which humans can no longer meaningfully oversee, correct or stop AI systems even after it becomes clear that a system is causing harm (see e.g. the International AI Safety Report), are reflected in only two of the surveyed works. EmbodiedGovBench tests whether a robot runtime honours human overrides, but not the ability or willingness of models to evade them. ForesightSafety Bench assesses misalignment and loss of control through text questions only. For non-physical agents, related behaviours have been evaluated directly: RepliBench measures autonomous replication capabilities, the Agent Matrix study evaluates self-replication risk in realistic scenarios, and AgentMisalignment measures the tendency towards misaligned behaviour. We did not find an embodied counterpart that evaluates resistance to being stopped, unprompted self-modification, concealment of actions, or evaluation awareness that arises without instruction.
